Hi Samantha / Aurora team,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — great discussion. To size a Dedicated pool that meets your cost and latency goals, we need a short telemetry and prompt-sample intake so our pre-sales sizing can be data-driven rather than heuristic.

Could you please provide the following by EOD next week if possible:
- 7 days of anonymized request telemetry (timestamps, model, prompt token counts, response token counts, status codes) — 1–2MB samples are fine.
- A small set (~50) of representative prompts + expected response lengths (CSV).
- Peak observed concurrent sessions and any known hourly/daypart peaks.
- Target latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99) and acceptable fallback policy (e.g., can you accept a higher-latency tail during bursts?)
- Any constraints: PCI/PHI, VPC-only traffic, preferred model family (e.g., Llama2-70B, Mistral), or quantized variants.

I've attached our redwood-sizing-template.xlsx — it has a short worksheet you can fill with burst/steady rates, concurrency, and sample prompt distribution. If you'd rather drop sample logs into the ops email (ops@aurorahealth.ai) or a secure S3 link, that works too.

Attachments: redwood-sizing-template.xlsx (worksheet)

If helpful, we can run a short walkthrough of the worksheet — I'm available Thurs/Fri afternoon PT.

Quick read of the 48h sample — thanks for sending, Sam. High level findings and a first-ballpark: 

Summary of telemetry (48h sample):
- Model mix: 62% klein-13B, 38% prod-70B.
- Prompt token distribution (tokens prompt -> fraction): p50=40, p90=180, p99=620.
- Response token distribution: p50=32, p90=150, p99=920.
- Sustained qps: ~18 qps (off-peak), observed peak short bursts to ~220 qps (~6x sustained) for ~5–8 minute windows.
- Typical session affinity: sessions are fairly sticky (KV reuse ~70%) which helps caching.

Initial sizing suggestion (conservative, can optimize later):
- Steady: 2 x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs (tenant-eq) to cover sustained 18 qps with buffer for normal day-to-day.
- Burst handling: allow autoscale up to 8 GPUs to cover short bursts to ~220 qps assuming aggressive batching and transient queuing; recommend burst policy with 3-minute cooldown.
- Per-GPU concurrency assumption: 20 concurrent short sessions for klein-13B with quantization; 6–8 concurrent heavy sessions for prod-70B.
- Latency SLOs: with above model mapping, expected p95 ~120–240ms depending on token length; p99 can spike during burst without autoscale.

Next steps we need from Aurora to tighten sizing:
- A longer 7-day sample if available (captures weekday vs weekend patterns).
- Clarify target p99 latency and business impact threshold for tail penalties.
- Any compliance constraints that would block cross-tenant batching or caching.

I'll draft a short proposal (Aurora-sizing-proposal-v1.pdf) that maps this into a committed Dedicated contract (GPU counts, expected cost bands) — ping me if you want a walkthrough.

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
